name: ProofPass – Safety Data Sheets (SDS) & GPSR Info
author: Adam Khalil

sections.description:
This plugin puts the safety data sheet (SDS, often still searched as MSDS) of each product where your customers look for it: on the WooCommerce product page, in the order email and on any WordPress page. The same goes for technical data sheets (TDS), declarations of performance, EU declarations of conformity and other product documents, and for the manufacturer and safety information that belongs to a product.

The documents come from ProofPass, a data sheet portal for manufacturers and dealers. You upload a PDF there once. ProofPass keeps every version, creates a QR code per product and delivers new versions to your customers with proof of delivery. The plugin links the current version each time, so no outdated PDF stays behind in your media library.

Start with the catalogue scan

Right after connecting, the plugin compares your WooCommerce catalogue with ProofPass: which products have their documents, which have none, and where the GPSR details (manufacturer, responsible person, safety information) are missing. The scan reads only, creates nothing and works in the free Basic plan.

Free in your theme

Every ProofPass plan includes a read key, the free Basic plan too. With it the documents appear in the design of your shop as real links, readable for search engines and screen readers, with the line “Provided via ProofPass” below them. You pay only for more products, for order reports or to remove the line.

Dealers: show the documents of your manufacturers

Dealers need no account of their own. Enter the ProofPass address of your manufacturer under Settings → ProofPass and leave the key empty: the plugin passes the GTIN or article number of each product to the ProofPass embed, which shows the manufacturer’s current documents. When the manufacturer publishes a new version, your product page shows it.

What you need

  • A ProofPass account, or only the ProofPass address of your manufacturer (embed). The Basic plan is free; the link “Create a free ProofPass account” is on the settings page.
  • Without an API key: the document list of a product, the document search and the product passport appear as the official ProofPass embed. That works in every plan, including Basic.
  • With an API key with the permission “Lesen” (every plan, Basic included): the documents are rendered in your theme as real links, readable for search engines and screen readers. The QR code, the single document button, the documents for your quote, the Proposition 65 warning, the email updates link and the document links in order emails need the key as well. A scan key runs the WooCommerce catalogue scan.
  • The optional order report needs a key with write permission (paid plans) and the data processing agreement concluded in ProofPass.
  • WooCommerce is optional. Easy Digital Downloads, SureCart, BigCommerce for WordPress and WP EasyCart are set up automatically, any other shop by its product post type. Blocks, shortcodes, the widget and page builder elements work on any WordPress site.

Safety data sheets and other documents of a product

  • Document list of one product: type, language, revision date, version and PDF link. Safety data sheets for the USA (OSHA HazCom) show their emergency phone number.
  • Single document button, for example “Safety data sheet (PDF)”, in the language of the page if it exists.
  • Document search of the whole catalogue by product name, article number or GTIN: a search form that works without JavaScript, results with their documents, pagination.
  • Documents for your quote: the documents of several products or of the cart, with a button to your own quote page.
  • Updates by email: a link to the subscription on ProofPass (double opt-in).

GPSR: manufacturer, responsible person, safety information

Below the documents the plugin shows the manufacturer with postal address and electronic address, the responsible person in the EU, the warnings and safety information of the product, and an active recall notice. These are the details the General Product Safety Regulation (GPSR) names for online offers. The plugin prints what you maintain in ProofPass; it does not check your offer and does not make a shop compliant.

Product passport and QR code

  • Product passport: identifiers (article number, GTIN, UFI, brand, model, batch, CE marking), documents, manufacturer, safety information and QR code on one page.
  • QR code of a product, linking to its documents on ProofPass.

Battery passport

The EU Battery Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 asks for a QR code on batteries from 18 February 2027, and for a battery passport for batteries for light means of transport (e-bikes, e-scooters), industrial batteries above 2 kWh and electric vehicle batteries. ProofPass has a template for it: the label data of Annex VI Part A, the passport data of Annex XIII per model, per batch and per single battery, each with its access level (public, persons with a legitimate interest, authorities). The product passport page on ProofPass shows the public part; the plugin links it from its product passport element and prints the QR code that leads there. ProofPass stores what you enter; it does not calculate the carbon footprint and does not read values from a battery management system.

Proposition 65

For products sold to California the plugin shows the Proposition 65 (Prop 65) warning exactly as the manufacturer stored it: above the add-to-cart button and with the item in cart and checkout (classic and block checkout), or anywhere as an element.

WooCommerce

  • Placement on the product page: own tab, collapsible section or open list in the summary, or below the add-to-cart button.
  • Mapping, first hit wins: the field “ProofPass product” (tab “ProofPass” in the product data), the GTIN or EAN (WooCommerce field, Germanized, Google for WooCommerce, CTX Feed, EAN for WooCommerce, WP-Lister, Yoast WooCommerce SEO, a product attribute or a meta key you name), the SKU as article number, the manufacturer part number. Variations can have their own documents; the list switches when a variation is chosen. A variable or grouped product without its own match shows the documents of its children.
  • Links to the documents of the bought products in the customer’s order emails and on the order-received page.
  • Catalogue scan (WooCommerce → ProofPass): which products are in ProofPass and which documents are missing, with a column and a filter “ProofPass” in the product list, a mapping screen with suggestions by name, and a hint when the catalogue is larger than your plan.
  • Optional order report (off by default): paid orders go to ProofPass in the background; ProofPass sends professional buyers the current safety data sheets and records the delivery. You decide who counts as professional: company name, VAT ID or customer role.
  • Compatible with High-Performance Order Storage, block themes and the cart and checkout blocks. Translated products (WPML, Polylang) use the identifiers of their original; the page language also comes from Weglot and TranslatePress.

Other shop systems

  • Easy Digital Downloads, SureCart, BigCommerce for WordPress and WP EasyCart: the plugin finds the ProofPass product by the GTIN (BigCommerce’s own field, or a custom field you name), then by the article number (SKU) of the shop product, and shows its documents on the product page.
  • Any other shop that keeps its products as a custom post type: choose the post type and the custom fields with article number and GTIN under Settings → ProofPass.
  • The catalogue scan covers these products as well (Tools → ProofPass; with WooCommerce active it stays under WooCommerce → ProofPass). Order emails and the order report are WooCommerce only.

Block editor, page builders, shortcodes

  • Block editor: block “ProofPass” with a variation per element, product search against your ProofPass catalogue and a live preview.
  • Elementor: eight widgets in the category “ProofPass”.
  • Beaver Builder: module “ProofPass”.
  • SiteOrigin Page Builder and classic themes: widget “ProofPass” for sidebars, footers and widget areas.
  • Bricks: element “ProofPass”. Divi and WPBakery: element “ProofPass” (see FAQ: these three are written against their documented APIs, not tested without a licence). In every builder the shortcodes work as well.
  • Shortcodes, with a generator button in the classic editor: [proofpass_documents], [proofpass_catalog], [proofpass_qr], [proofpass_document], [proofpass_passport], [proofpass_quote], [proofpass_prop65], [proofpass_updates]. [proofpass] works as in version 1.

All of them render through one core on the server, so the output is the same everywhere.

Built with care

  • The API key stays on your server; it is never printed in HTML or passed to JavaScript.
  • Stale-while-revalidate cache: answers are kept for 6 hours (adjustable), then served while a background job asks ProofPass again. A page view makes at most one request to ProofPass. “Clear cache” button and wp proofpass cache flush.
  • No JavaScript on the front end, except a few lines on variable products whose variations have their own documents, and the optional Proposition 65 region check. The stylesheet loads only where an element renders. Logical CSS properties, so right-to-left languages work.
  • Accessible markup: table captions, labelled links and form fields, a search landmark, page navigation with aria-current.
  • Document language follows the page language (WPML and Polylang included) and falls back to the other languages.
  • WP-CLI: wp proofpass status, wp proofpass scan, wp proofpass map, wp proofpass cache flush.
  • Site Health test (connection, key permission, data processing agreement for order reports) and a suggested text for your privacy policy.
  • No tracking, no cookies. One admin notice while the plugin is not set up, on the dashboard and the plugins screen only, dismissible.
  • The line “Provided via ProofPass” is off unless you switch it on. Every plan below Pro includes it; to render the documents in your theme in those plans you agree to show it, otherwise the plugin uses the ProofPass embed, which shows it itself.

External services

This plugin connects to ProofPass, a service of EA Digital Solutions e.U., Liebenauer Hauptstraße 41, 8041 Graz, Austria. It cannot show anything without it.

Every request from your server (1 to 3 below, and the connection test) also carries the host name of your site and the major versions of WordPress, WooCommerce and PHP (headers X-ProofPass-Site and X-ProofPass-Env), so ProofPass can count the installations in use and keep them compatible.

1. ProofPass API (your server, with an API key)

  • What it is for: reads the current documents and manufacturer information of products, the product search of the catalogue and the plan of your account (to explain what the plugin can do).
  • What is sent: your API key (HTTP header Authorization: Bearer …), the product identifiers being looked up (GTIN, article number/SKU, ProofPass product ID, slug or short code) and search words. Your server’s IP address is visible to ProofPass. No visitor data is sent.
  • When: when a page with a ProofPass element is viewed and the cache has no fresh answer (at most once per page view; the rest in the background), when an editor searches for a product, and when you click “Test connection”.
  • Address: https://www.proofpass.eu/api/v1.

2. ProofPass order report (your server, only when switched on)

  • What it is for: ProofPass sends the buyer of a paid order the current safety data sheets of the ordered products and records the delivery; professional buyers are added to the manufacturer’s distribution list in ProofPass.
  • What is sent: your write key, the order number, the identifiers of the ordered products, whether the buyer counts as professional, and the buyer’s billing email address, company, name and language.
  • When: once per order, in the background after the order status changes to “processing” or “completed”, with up to five retries after an error.
  • Address: https://www.proofpass.eu/api/v1/orders.

3. ProofPass catalogue scan (your server, when you start it)

  • What it is for: shows which products of your shop (WooCommerce or another shop system set up under Settings → ProofPass) are in ProofPass and which documents are missing.
  • What is sent: your key and, for each product, its GTIN, SKU and name. ProofPass does not store the list.
  • When: when you click “Scan catalogue”, run wp proofpass scan, or the first time “Test connection” succeeds with WooCommerce active.
  • Address: https://www.proofpass.eu/api/v1/catalog/scan.

4. Files and pages of ProofPass in the visitor’s browser

  • The ProofPass embed (frame or the script widget.js), when the output is set to the embed or no API key is saved: the browser loads it from www.proofpass.eu and sends the address of the frame (manufacturer, language, product identifier) and, as with every web request, the visitor’s IP address and browser data. Inside the frame ProofPass counts search terms and document opens anonymously for the manufacturer (no cookie, no identifier).
  • PDF documents, the QR code image of the elements “QR code” and “Product passport”, and the links to product pages on ProofPass load from www.proofpass.eu when the visitor opens or sees them.
  • Proposition 65 region check, only if you switch it on: the browser asks www.proofpass.eu/api/us/warnung whether the warning applies at the visitor’s location and, when the warning becomes visible, posts the page address, a random page-view ID and a signed token to www.proofpass.eu/api/us/anzeige. ProofPass stores time, country and region from its own request headers, the page and the page-view ID; no IP address, no user agent, no cookie.
  • No cookies are set by any of these.

About the script mode

In the embed mode “Script” the page loads widget.js from www.proofpass.eu. This is the embed script of the ProofPass service itself, not a library from a CDN, and it only builds the frame that shows the documents. It is printed where the element stands, with wp_get_script_tag(), because it reads its settings from its own data- attributes. Its address carries ?via=wordpress, so ProofPass can count script embeds that come from this plugin; nothing else about your site or the visitor is added. The default embed mode “Frame (iframe)” loads no script. The plugin never downloads or runs code from ProofPass on your server.

The connection test without API key requests https://www.proofpass.eu/einbetten/<manufacturer>/widget.js?via=wordpress once from your server. The link “Create a free ProofPass account” opens the sign-up page of ProofPass with the parameter cta=wordpress.plugin.settings, so ProofPass can tell that the sign-up came from the plugin; nothing about your site is sent.

  • Terms of service: https://www.proofpass.eu/agb
  • Privacy policy: https://www.proofpass.eu/datenschutz
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the Plugins screen (search for “ProofPass”), or upload the folder proofpass to /wp-content/plugins/, and activate it.
  2. Open Settings → ProofPass. No account yet: “Create a free ProofPass account”. Upload your safety data sheets and other documents in ProofPass.
  3. Enter your manufacturer (your ProofPass address https://www.proofpass.eu/hersteller/your-company or only your-company) and an API key (ProofPass dashboard → Einbinden → API-Schlüssel; a read key is included in every plan), then click “Test connection”. With WooCommerce the catalogue scan runs right after. Dealers enter the address of their manufacturer and leave the key empty.
  4. Add the block “ProofPass” to a page, use a page builder element or a shortcode. With WooCommerce the documents appear on the product page by themselves.
sections.faq:
How do I add a safety data sheet (SDS) to a WooCommerce product?

Upload the PDF to the product in ProofPass and give the WooCommerce product the same GTIN or SKU. The plugin then shows the safety data sheet on the product page by itself. Products without a matching number get the field “ProofPass product” or the mapping screen.

Do I need a paid ProofPass plan?

No. The embed, the catalogue scan and documents rendered in your theme work in the free Basic plan (up to 10 products), with the line “Provided via ProofPass”. A paid plan is needed for more products, for order reports and, from the Pro plan, to remove the line.

I am a dealer. Can I show the documents of my manufacturers?

Yes, without an account of your own. Enter the ProofPass address of the manufacturer under Settings → ProofPass and leave the API key empty. The plugin passes the GTIN or article number of each product to the ProofPass embed, which shows the manufacturer’s current documents. The settings hold one manufacturer per site.

Does it show the EU battery passport?

The battery data lives on the product passport page on ProofPass: the template for Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 with the label data of Annex VI Part A and the passport data of Annex XIII, per model, batch or single battery. The plugin’s product passport element and the QR code link that page. Data for persons with a legitimate interest and for authorities stays behind the access levels in ProofPass. The plugin does not check whether your data is complete or correct.

Does it work without WooCommerce?

Yes. The block, the shortcodes, the widget and the page builder elements work on any WordPress site, for example as a download page with the document search of your whole catalogue. With Easy Digital Downloads, SureCart, BigCommerce for WordPress or WP EasyCart the documents appear on the product pages by themselves; for another shop you choose its product post type under Settings → ProofPass. Easy Digital Downloads and SureCart were run with this release, BigCommerce and WP EasyCart are written against their source code and were not run. Ecwid and ShopWP draw their product pages outside WordPress templates: there you place a block or shortcode with the product.

Does the plugin make my shop GPSR compliant?

No. It shows the documents and the manufacturer, responsible person and safety information you maintain in ProofPass. Whether an offer meets the GPSR depends on your data and your products. The plugin is not legal advice.

Can I upload the PDFs to the WordPress media library instead?

No. The documents live in ProofPass, so there is one current version with its history, and the plugin links it. A PDF in the media library would stay as it is when the manufacturer publishes a new version.

Where does a Proposition 65 warning come from?

From the product in ProofPass, with the wording the manufacturer stored. The plugin shows it on the product page and in cart and checkout; a product without a stored warning shows none. The optional region check lets ProofPass apply the region the manufacturer set.

Can I remove the line “Provided via ProofPass”?

It is off by default. Every plan below Pro includes it: in the embed ProofPass shows it; for documents rendered in your theme you agree to show it under Settings → ProofPass, otherwise the plugin uses the embed. From the Pro plan it is optional.

Which page builders are supported?

Block editor (also in the Site Editor and inside a Query Loop), Elementor, Beaver Builder and SiteOrigin Page Builder are tested with this release. Bricks, Divi (module API of Divi 4, which Divi 5 runs in its compatibility mode) and WPBakery (vc_map) are written against their documented developer APIs but were not run, because they are commercial. Oxygen and Breakdance take the shortcodes or the widget. If the element does not appear there, put a shortcode such as [proofpass_documents product="art:SN-310"] into a Code or Text module; that always works.

How does the WooCommerce mapping work?

First the field “ProofPass product” of the product or variation, then the GTIN, then the SKU as article number. A variation tries its own identifiers first, then those of its parent. Developers can change the order with the filter proofpass_product_lookup_keys. The scan and the mapping screen (WooCommerce → ProofPass → Mapping) help with products that are not found.

Where does the plugin read the GTIN (EAN)?

From the WooCommerce field (since WooCommerce 9.2), from a meta key you enter under Settings → ProofPass, from the fields of Product GTIN (EAN, UPC, ISBN) for WooCommerce, EAN for WooCommerce, Germanized, Google for WooCommerce, CTX Feed, WooCommerce UPC, EAN, and ISBN, WP-Lister for eBay and Amazon and Yoast WooCommerce SEO, from _gtin and _ean, and from a product attribute named gtin, ean or upc.

A new document version does not show up.

Answers are cached for 6 hours by default, then refreshed in the background. Save the product, click “Clear cache” under Settings → ProofPass or run wp proofpass cache flush.

Does the plugin set cookies or track visitors?

No. The optional Proposition 65 region check sends ProofPass, from the visitor’s browser, a random page-view ID and the page address when the warning was visible, and ProofPass stores country and region; no IP address and no cookie. It is off by default.

Can visitors subscribe to new versions?

Yes, with the element “Updates by email” or the link under the document list. It opens the product page on ProofPass, where the visitor subscribes with double opt-in; the address then appears in your distribution list in ProofPass. The plugin itself collects no personal data.

Which data does an order report send?

The order number, GTIN or SKU (or the ProofPass product ID) of each ordered product, whether the buyer counts as professional, and the buyer’s billing email address, company, name and the site language. No prices, no addresses, no payment data. ProofPass accepts order reports only after the current data processing agreement is concluded in its dashboard; until then the plugin says so in its settings, in Site Health and in the order note.

Does the plugin store personal data?

No. The order report job carries only the order ID and reads the address from the WooCommerce order when it runs. The plugin keeps only a status per order (queued, done, skipped, failed).
sections.changelog:
2.2.0

  • Documents in your theme work in every ProofPass plan: a read key is part of the free Basic plan too (with the line “Provided via ProofPass”). Messages and help texts say so.
  • Messages: a refused request names what is missing (order reports need a paid plan) instead of the whole API.
  • Description: catalogue scan first, dealers without an account of their own, battery passport.
  • Plan names: Basic and Complete in every language, as on proofpass.eu (they were Basis and Komplett in some translations).

2.1.1

  • Live Preview on wordpress.org: try the plugin with WooCommerce and a demo product in WordPress Playground.
  • Requests from your server to ProofPass now name the site (host name) and the WordPress, WooCommerce and PHP versions in two headers, as described under External services. The script embed (widget.js) is loaded with ?via=wordpress; the frame embed is unchanged.

2.1.0

  • Other shop systems: Easy Digital Downloads, SureCart, BigCommerce for WordPress and WP EasyCart are set up automatically; any other shop by its product post type and custom fields. The catalogue scan covers them (Tools → ProofPass).
  • WooCommerce: GTIN and EAN from more plugins (Germanized, Google for WooCommerce, CTX Feed, WP-Lister, Yoast WooCommerce SEO and others), from product attributes, and the manufacturer part number. Variable and grouped products show the documents of their children. “Documents in the cart” works in the cart block. Translated products use the identifiers of their original. All product types are scanned.
  • Caching and optimisation plugins: the scripts no longer depend on their load order (deferred, delayed or combined scripts); a page whose documents are still loading is not stored in a page cache.
  • New: classic widget “ProofPass” (sidebars, SiteOrigin Page Builder), Bricks element, block usable inside a Query Loop, colour and typography settings for the block.
  • Themes: readable in dark sections, visible keyboard focus, larger touch targets, colours adjustable through CSS custom properties.
  • Accessibility: table caption and headers, link texts that name the document, language marked on documents in another language.
  • Fixed: the Elementor widget “Single document” always showed the safety data sheet. Feeds no longer contain the search form or the embed.
  • New name in the directory: ProofPass – Safety Data Sheets (SDS) & GPSR Info.

2.0.0

  • New: documents rendered in your theme as real links (API key), for every element; the embed stays available per element and as the fallback.
  • New elements: document search of the whole catalogue, QR code, single document button, product passport, documents for your quote, Proposition 65 warning, updates by email.
  • New: block “ProofPass” with variations, product search and live preview (the block of version 1 keeps working); Elementor widgets; Beaver Builder module; Divi module and WPBakery element (untested, see FAQ); shortcode generator in the classic editor.
  • New WooCommerce placements (tab, collapsible section, summary, below the add-to-cart button), “ProofPass” tab in the product data, mapping per variation, documents in order emails and on the order-received page, documents of the cart.
  • New: Proposition 65 warnings on the product page and in cart and checkout, US safety data sheets with emergency number.
  • New: column and filter “ProofPass” in the product list from the scan, mapping screen with suggestions by name, WP-CLI commands, Site Health test, privacy policy text.
  • New: order report counts chosen customer roles as professional; the settings, Site Health and the order note say when the data processing agreement is missing.
  • New: onboarding with a free sign-up link; the scan is the first screen after connecting.
  • Cache: stale-while-revalidate with background refresh, at most one request to ProofPass per page view.
  • Settings of version 1 are kept: existing sites keep the embed and the product tab until you change the output.
  • Translations are no longer bundled; they come as language packs from translate.wordpress.org.

1.1.1

  • Order report: when ProofPass is still processing the same order (HTTP 409), the plugin asks again later instead of giving up. A repeated report no longer leaves the note that no product has a current safety data sheet.

1.1.0

  • New: optional order report. Paid WooCommerce orders go to ProofPass in the background (Action Scheduler, WP-Cron as fallback); ProofPass sends professional buyers the current safety data sheets and records the delivery.
  • New: WooCommerce → ProofPass scan.
  • The connection messages name a key that lacks the permission for a request.

1.0.0

  • First release: settings page with connection test, shortcode [proofpass], block “ProofPass data sheets”, WooCommerce product tab with automatic mapping (GTIN, SKU, override field), API v1 document list with cache, embed fallback, German translation.

  • Compatible with High-Performance Order Storage, block themes and the cart and checkout blocks. Translated products (WPML, Polylang) use the identifiers of their original; the page language also comes from Weglot and TranslatePress.

Other shop systems

  • Easy Digital Downloads, SureCart, BigCommerce for WordPress and WP EasyCart: the plugin finds the ProofPass product by the GTIN (BigCommerce’s own field, or a custom field you name), then by the article number (SKU) of the shop product, and shows its documents on the product page.
  • Any other shop that keeps its products as a custom post type: choose the post type and the custom fields with article number and GTIN under Settings → ProofPass.
  • The catalogue scan covers these products as well (Tools → ProofPass; with WooCommerce active it stays under WooCommerce → ProofPass). Order emails and the order report are WooCommerce only.

Block editor, page builders, shortcodes

  • Block editor: block “ProofPass” with a variation per element, product search against your ProofPass catalogue and a live preview.
  • Elementor: eight widgets in the category “ProofPass”.
  • Beaver Builder: module “ProofPass”.
  • SiteOrigin Page Builder and classic themes: widget “ProofPass” for sidebars, footers and widget areas.
  • Bricks: element “ProofPass”. Divi and WPBakery: element “ProofPass” (see FAQ: these three are written against their documented APIs, not tested without a licence). In every builder the shortcodes work as well.
  • Shortcodes, with a generator button in the classic editor: [proofpass_documents], [proofpass_catalog], [proofpass_qr], [proofpass_document], [proofpass_passport], [proofpass_quote], [proofpass_prop65], [proofpass_updates]. [proofpass] works as in version 1.

All of them render through one core on the server, so the output is the same everywhere.

Built with care

  • The API key stays on your server; it is never printed in HTML or passed to JavaScript.
  • Stale-while-revalidate cache: answers are kept for 6 hours (adjustable), then served while a background job asks ProofPass again. A page view makes at most one request to ProofPass. “Clear cache” button and wp proofpass cache flush.
  • No JavaScript on the front end, except a few lines on variable products whose variations have their own documents, and the optional Proposition 65 region check. The stylesheet loads only where an element renders. Logical CSS properties, so right-to-left languages work.
  • Accessible markup: table captions, labelled links and form fields, a search landmark, page navigation with aria-current.
  • Document language follows the page language (WPML and Polylang included) and falls back to the other languages.
  • WP-CLI: wp proofpass status, wp proofpass scan, wp proofpass map, wp proofpass cache flush.
  • Site Health test (connection, key permission, data processing agreement for order reports) and a suggested text for your privacy policy.
  • No tracking, no cookies. One admin notice while the plugin is not set up, on the dashboard and the plugins screen only, dismissible.
  • The line “Provided via ProofPass” is off unless you switch it on. Every plan below Pro includes it; to render the documents in your theme in those plans you agree to show it, otherwise the plugin uses the ProofPass embed, which shows it itself.

External services

This plugin connects to ProofPass, a service of EA Digital Solutions e.U., Liebenauer Hauptstraße 41, 8041 Graz, Austria. It cannot show anything without it.

Every request from your server (1 to 3 below, and the connection test) also carries the host name of your site and the major versions of WordPress, WooCommerce and PHP (headers X-ProofPass-Site and X-ProofPass-Env), so ProofPass can count the installations in use and keep them compatible.

1. ProofPass API (your server, with an API key)

  • What it is for: reads the current documents and manufacturer information of products, the product search of the catalogue and the plan of your account (to explain what the plugin can do).
  • What is sent: your API key (HTTP header Authorization: Bearer …), the product identifiers being looked up (GTIN, article number/SKU, ProofPass product ID, slug or short code) and search words. Your server’s IP address is visible to ProofPass. No visitor data is sent.
  • When: when a page with a ProofPass element is viewed and the cache has no fresh answer (at most once per page view; the rest in the background), when an editor searches for a product, and when you click “Test connection”.
  • Address: https://www.proofpass.eu/api/v1.

2. ProofPass order report (your server, only when switched on)

  • What it is for: ProofPass sends the buyer of a paid order the current safety data sheets of the ordered products and records the delivery; professional buyers are added to the manufacturer’s distribution list in ProofPass.
  • What is sent: your write key, the order number, the identifiers of the ordered products, whether the buyer counts as professional, and the buyer’s billing email address, company, name and language.
  • When: once per order, in the background after the order status changes to “processing” or “completed”, with up to five retries after an error.
  • Address: https://www.proofpass.eu/api/v1/orders.

3. ProofPass catalogue scan (your server, when you start it)

  • What it is for: shows which products of your shop (WooCommerce or another shop system set up under Settings → ProofPass) are in ProofPass and which documents are missing.
  • What is sent: your key and, for each product, its GTIN, SKU and name. ProofPass does not store the list.
  • When: when you click “Scan catalogue”, run wp proofpass scan, or the first time “Test connection” succeeds with WooCommerce active.
  • Address: https://www.proofpass.eu/api/v1/catalog/scan.

4. Files and pages of ProofPass in the visitor’s browser

  • The ProofPass embed (frame or the script widget.js), when the output is set to the embed or no API key is saved: the browser loads it from www.proofpass.eu and sends the address of the frame (manufacturer, language, product identifier) and, as with every web request, the visitor’s IP address and browser data. Inside the frame ProofPass counts search terms and document opens anonymously for the manufacturer (no cookie, no identifier).
  • PDF documents, the QR code image of the elements “QR code” and “Product passport”, and the links to product pages on ProofPass load from www.proofpass.eu when the visitor opens or sees them.
  • Proposition 65 region check, only if you switch it on: the browser asks www.proofpass.eu/api/us/warnung whether the warning applies at the visitor’s location and, when the warning becomes visible, posts the page address, a random page-view ID and a signed token to www.proofpass.eu/api/us/anzeige. ProofPass stores time, country and region from its own request headers, the page and the page-view ID; no IP address, no user agent, no cookie.
  • No cookies are set by any of these.

About the script mode

In the embed mode “Script” the page loads widget.js from www.proofpass.eu. This is the embed script of the ProofPass service itself, not a library from a CDN, and it only builds the frame that shows the documents. It is printed where the element stands, with wp_get_script_tag(), because it reads its settings from its own data- attributes. Its address carries ?via=wordpress, so ProofPass can count script embeds that come from this plugin; nothing else about your site or the visitor is added. The default embed mode “Frame (iframe)” loads no script. The plugin never downloads or runs code from ProofPass on your server.

The connection test without API key requests https://www.proofpass.eu/einbetten/<manufacturer>/widget.js?via=wordpress once from your server. The link “Create a free ProofPass account” opens the sign-up page of ProofPass with the parameter cta=wordpress.plugin.settings, so ProofPass can tell that the sign-up came from the plugin; nothing about your site is sent.

  • Terms of service: https://www.proofpass.eu/agb
  • Privacy policy: https://www.proofpass.eu/datenschutz
